subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `cron run` be a non-consuming operator/verification action that never deletes one-shot jobs or changes scheduler counters, retry state, enabled state, or pending schedule slots?
rationale: The code can mechanically enforce either behavior, but changing manual-run semantics affects existing operator workflows and cannot be inferred safely from the implementation alone.

options.title: Adopt observational manual runs
options.body: Keep this PR's internal-origin model so public manual runs record outcomes but leave scheduler-owned state and one-shot consumption to timer and watcher-terminal paths.

options.title: Keep manual runs consuming
options.body: Retain current semantics and close this branch if a successful manual run is intended to consume `deleteAfterRun` jobs and scheduler state.

options.title: Expose an explicit consuming operation
options.body: Make ordinary manual runs observational while designing a separately documented, opt-in operator action for intentionally consuming a scheduled one-shot.

recommendation.title: Adopt observational manual runs
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's internal-origin model so public manual runs record outcomes but leave scheduler-owned state and one-shot consumption to timer and watcher-terminal paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work owns the manual-run scheduling and recovery semantics this decision changes.
